note: MANIFEST.json parses to a non-empty array wrapping what would otherwise be a sound manifest. DD-R01 refuses it as not a JSON object, and section 2.2 says the refusal is recorded under MANIFEST.<stamp>.run.json with the stamp taken from started_at, because a non-object has no written_at to read. Added in DD2 v5 for the second review's P-1: the record namer guarded only a falsy non-object, so a truthy one raised instead of being recorded. The suite now catches the class; a tool that raises here prints got exception/<Name> -> MISMATCH.
